stemMd: A substance has mass $M(t)=160(\frac12)^{t/6}$ grams after $t$ hours. After how many hours is its mass 20 grams?
explanationMd: The mass ratio is 20/160=1/8=(1/2)³. Therefore t/6=3, giving t=18 hours. Three halvings take 160 to 80 to 40 to 20.

distractorRationale.d: The ratio of masses is not the number of half-life intervals.
